correctness.rationale: Every surviving unserved vertex is in a controller-free gap and must be separated from each endpoint controller by an attack on each of two disjoint paths. Inclusion-exclusion counts these attacks exactly under a uniform fixed-size subset, for all boundary cases. Expected served count subtracts deleted and surviving unserved vertices from n. Pascal identity gives the exact second difference d*binom(n-d-2,r-2), which is nonnegative; pairwise gap smoothing gives optimal balanced gaps. For two deletions it is positive at every feasible smoothing step, and any law with positive two-deletion mass inherits strictness. For independent failures the exact penalty has second difference d*p^2*(1-p)^d>0. Standalone exact component enumeration n<=9 and integer difference verification n<=31 replay successfully; finite checks do not replace the proof.

value.rationale: The theorem determines a single robust optimal controller geometry for every exchangeable vertex-failure law on a ring, even with correlated attacks and unknown failure-count distribution. The exact penalty and equality conditions quantify the reliability cost of unbalanced controller layouts, extending beyond existing two-controller strategic-equilibrium examples. This resolves a motivated average-case design problem in the same graph-division model with fully finite-n statements.
